title: Machine computing input length
statement: There exist a natural number $K$, a finite state set, a deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet with $K+1$ work tapes, entry and exit states, and a constant $C$. From any configuration on a binary input $x$ with the machine in the entry state, input head at position $1$, tape $0$ blank on the interval from one cell before its head through the binary representation of $|x|$, and every other work tape entirely blank, the machine reaches its exit state at some time $t \le C(|x|+1)$. It does not reach the exit state earlier, every work-tape head stays within distance $C(|x|+1)$ of its initial position through time $t$, and at time $t$ tape $0$ holds the binary representation of $|x|$ starting at its initial head position, with all other cells and configuration data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The initial state is the entry state and the input head is at position $1$
Tape $0$ is blank on the specified interval
Every other work tape is entirely blank
The exit state is not reached before time $t$
All work-tape head displacements through time $t$ are at most $C(|x|+1)$
The final tape and configuration contents are as specified
